nodes.description: Owner address of the Owned contract; controls privileged functions.
Pending owner address set by transferOwnership, confirmed by acceptOwnership.
Token symbol string, set to 'Shih' in the constructor.
Token name string, set to 'Shit Tzu Doge' in the constructor.
Token decimals, set to 18 in the constructor.
Total token supply stored on deployment.
Mapping of holder address to token balance.
Nested mapping of owner to spender to allowance.
Owned constructor assigning owner = msg.sender.
onlyOwner function that stages a new owner in newOwner.
Confirms ownership transfer when called by newOwner; clears newOwner.
Token constructor that mints the whole supply to a fixed address.
Returns _totalSupply minus balances[address(0)] using an unchecked subtraction.
Returns the balance of a given token owner.
Transfers tokens from msg.sender to a recipient using safeSub/safeAdd.
Sets the allowance of a spender from msg.sender.
Spends an allowance to move tokens between two accounts.
Returns the remaining allowance for a spender.
Sets allowance and then calls receiveApproval on the spender contract.
Payable fallback that unconditionally reverts, refusing ETH.
onlyOwner rescue function that pulls arbitrary ERC20 tokens to owner.
Overflow-checked addition helper.
Underflow-checked subtraction helper.
Overflow-checked multiplication helper.
Division helper rejecting a zero divisor.
msg.sender: caller-controlled address used for auth and balance accounting.
External call to ApproveAndCallFallBack(spender).receiveApproval after allowance is written.
External call ERC20Interface(tokenAddress).transfer(owner, tokens) to an arbitrary token contract.
New owner address argument of transferOwnership.

Spender argument of allowance.

edges.reason: msg.sender is read in the Owned constructor to initialize the owner.
Owned constructor writes owner = msg.sender.
onlyOwner modifier compares msg.sender with owner before transferOwnership runs.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner to authorize the transfer.
transfer uses msg.sender as the debited balance holder.
transferFrom uses msg.sender as the allowance spender key.
approveAndCall writes the allowance for msg.sender and forwards it as callback argument.
transferOwnership writes the supplied address into newOwner.
owner is read by the onlyOwner guard on transferOwnership.
acceptOwnership assigns owner = newOwner.
acceptOwnership resets newOwner to address(0).
acceptOwnership reads newOwner for the authorization check.
totalSupply reads the _totalSupply state variable.
Shih constructor mints _totalSupply to the fixed holder address.
Constructor initializes the symbol state variable.
Constructor initializes the name state variable.
Constructor initializes the decimals state variable.
totalSupply reads balances[address(0)] as the burn adjustment.
balanceOf returns the balances mapping entry.
transfer reads and writes balances for sender and recipient.
transferFrom reads and writes balances for from and to.
approve writes allowed[msg.sender][spender].
transferFrom decrements allowed[from][msg.sender].
allowance returns allowed[tokenOwner][spender].
approveAndCall writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] before the external call.
transferAnyERC20Token reads owner as both the guard and the transfer destination.
approveAndCall invokes an arbitrary spender contract after updating the allowance state.
The callee contract can re-enter approveAndCall through the receiveApproval callback.
Re-entrant execution can re-write the allowed mapping while the first call is still in flight.
transferAnyERC20Token performs an external call to an arbitrary token contract.
Rescued tokens are sent to the owner address.
totalSupply performs an unchecked subtraction that can underflow.
_totalSupply is the minuend of the unchecked subtraction.
balances[address(0)] is the subtrahend and is not validated.
The _newOwner parameter flows into the newOwner state variable.
The transfer recipient parameter flows into the credited balance and Transfer event.
The transfer amount parameter flows into safeSub/safeAdd balance updates.
The spender parameter is written into the allowed mapping.
The allowance amount parameter is written into the allowed mapping.
The from parameter is debited in transferFrom.
The to parameter is credited in transferFrom.
The tokens parameter flows into balance and allowance accounting.
The tokenOwner parameter indexes the allowed mapping.
The spender parameter indexes the allowed mapping.
The spender parameter is the allowance key written by approveAndCall.
The spender parameter determines the external contract that is called back.
The tokens parameter is written as the allowance of the spender.
The data bytes parameter is carried through approveAndCall.
The data bytes parameter is forwarded verbatim into the external receiveApproval call.
The tokenAddress parameter selects the external contract to call.
The tokenAddress parameter is cast to ERC20Interface for the external call.
The tokens parameter is the amount requested from the external token.
The tokens parameter is passed to the external transfer call.
The tokenOwner parameter indexes the balances mapping.
Local variable c is the result of the guarded addition in safeAdd.
Local variable c is the result of the guarded subtraction in safeSub.
Local variable success is returned by transfer after balance updates.

normalization_plan.reason: The parameter only carries its value into the transferOwnership function's state write, so it can be folded into that function node.
The recipient parameter has no independent behavior and is consumed entirely by transfer.
The amount parameter only feeds the balance arithmetic inside transfer.
The spender parameter is used only as an index write inside approve.
The allowance amount parameter is used only inside approve.
The from parameter is only used for balance/allowance indexing inside transferFrom.
The to parameter is only used for the credited balance inside transferFrom.
The tokens parameter is consumed by the safeSub/safeAdd calls inside transferFrom.
The tokenOwner parameter is only used to read the allowed mapping in allowance.
The spender parameter is only used to read the allowed mapping in allowance.
The spender parameter drives the allowance write and the callback target of approveAndCall.
The tokens parameter is only used as the allowance value inside approveAndCall.
The data bytes are forwarded unchanged into the external receiveApproval call, so the parameter belongs with that unsafe operation.
The tokenAddress parameter only selects the target of the rescue call inside transferAnyERC20Token.
The tokens parameter is only passed through to the external transfer inside transferAnyERC20Token.
The tokenOwner parameter is only used to read the balances mapping in balanceOf.
The local c exists solely as the checked result of safeAdd and has no independent meaning.
The local c exists solely as the checked result of safeSub and has no independent meaning.
The success flag is a constant return of transfer and can be absorbed into that function node.
